doc.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Recording quickly in the studio
summary: The Swing 7 CD took two days; first takes and spontaneity, as with Ruby Braff.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: How much time would you get, or did you get, in the studio, to do a production like this. I mean you’ve got fourteen cuts on there.
Yeah. We did it, including rehearsal, two days.

Yeah. Before this last CD that we did we used to get together the day before and rehearse and then come in the studio the next day and play, and then for two days. But this time we decided to rehearse on the spot. And we found that we had the tape running even during the rehearsal as we ran at first, and these guys could read so well that it just, even the first take on rehearsal, we used several of those. And once in a while we’d say let’s do another one. But I don’t like to do too many.
Yeah. Well I guess that’s been, when you look back in the history of jazz recordings, they’re usually done fairly quickly.

Well I think it should be. I don’t think — for example I did a thing with Ruby [Braff] about two or three years ago, and one take, right through, the whole thing. I mean no second chances. You better do it right the first time. Because Ruby doesn’t like to do them more than once either. Mistakes and all, if there’s a little slur here or something, go with it. And there’s something to be said about that. It’s spontaneous. That’s what jazz is anyway.
